recognize_zh: 視野中有三顆細胞質充滿粗大橘紅色顆粒、核為雙葉或分葉的嗜酸性球（eosinophil），左側另有一顆核深紫、細胞質淡藍的淋巴球可作大小與顏色對照。
features: Three granulocytes slightly larger than red cells, each with cytoplasm packed with coarse, uniform orange-red granules
Nuclei bilobed to irregularly lobated with condensed, clumped chromatin; granules do not obscure the nucleus
Left-sided lymphocyte with a round-to-notched nucleus, coarse chromatin and a moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm
Background normocytic, normochromic red cells without significant poikilocytosis; rare platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with a small number of platelets. Three eosinophils are present, each with a bilobed to lobated nucleus and abundant cytoplasm filled with coarse, refractile orange-red granules. A small mature lymphocyte with a round, slightly indented nucleus and a modest rim of pale blue cytoplasm is present at the left for comparison. No immature or dysplastic cells are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with mature eosinophils; clustering of three in one field raises the possibility of eosinophilia, which should be confirmed by absolute count.

ddx.vs: Basophil granules are dark purple-black, larger and irregular and typically obscure the nucleus, whereas eosinophil granules are uniform orange-red and leave the nucleus visible.
Toxic granules are dark purple-blue and scattered in pale pink cytoplasm of a multilobed nucleus, not the densely packed orange-red granules seen here.
An eosinophilic myelocyte has a round, non-lobed nucleus and may contain some dark basophilic-staining immature granules, unlike these mature bilobed forms.
